text:
The data point to October 2010. Unemployment is 9.6%, which matches September–October 2010, and core CPI is near 0.95%, a record low reached around then. The fed funds rate is about 0.19% and the 10-year yield is 2.52%.

The 1-month equity return of +9% fits October 2010, but it fits September 2010 better, when US equities rose about 9%. The 10-year yield was around 2.5% at the end of September 2010 and 2.6% at the end of October. The 6-month equity return of -2.1% fits September, because equities were down from the April 2010 high through the end of September. The VIX at 23.25 also fits September 2010, when it closed near 23.5.

The payroll 3-month average of -94k fits the data as published then. Headline CPI of 1.2% is consistent with September 2010. The 20-year-plus Treasury return of -2.5% over the month is odd for September, but the other cues are strong enough.

I settle on September 2010.
